subject: POC MAP: Infrastructure Decisions & Owners (VPC, SSO, KMS)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Maria Delgado <maria.delgado@pangeaanalytics.com>, Tomas Rivera <tomas.rivera@pangeaanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC MAP: Infrastructure Decisions & Owners (VPC, SSO, KMS)

Hi Maria / Tomas —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion I’m attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the POC environment milestones so we can lock owners and any blocking dependencies. High-level asks below; please confirm owners or flag changes by EOD Monday so we can hit the proposed staging target.

POC target close: 2027-04-15 (target for initial evaluation, not final contract)

Key milestone: POC environment provisioning (staging) — dependencies and suggested owners
- VPC peering and routing: Pangea networking team -> owner: Tomas Rivera (Pangea); Redwood networking lead -> Ben Carter
- IP allowlists (ingress egress): Pangea security -> Maria Delgado; Redwood infra -> Karthik Iyer
- SSO/SAML (identity): Primary candidate: Okta. Pangea to confirm IdP details and SCIM support; owner: Maria
- Secrets / KMS: Customer keys vs Redwood-managed keys? Pangea preference affects timeline; suggested owner: Pangea security (Maria) + Redwood infra ops (Laura Bennett)
- Test plan & connectivity verification: Redwood to run connectivity smoke on 3/12; owner: Ben

Open decisions we need on or before 2027-03-12 call:
1) SSO approach: customer-managed Okta SAML integration or temporary test accounts? (affects timeline 1–2 weeks)
2) KMS/secrets model: bring-your-own-CMK vs Redwood-managed envelope keys (affects audit + procurement)
3) Network path: do you prefer VPC peering or a transit VPN for initial POC?

Next steps / asks (actionable):
- Maria: confirm IdP (Okta) and whether SCIM/provisioning will be available by 3/12.
- Tomas: share CIDR ranges for the staging VPC and preferred peering window.
- Ben / Karthik: we’ll draft a minimal firewall/IP allowlist doc and a short connectivity checklist for your security team.

Attachments: POC_MAP_v1_kp_comments.xlsx (MAP w/ milestones), poc-network-stub.png (carry-forward diagram)

I’ll update the MAP with owners once I have your confirmations and send an invite for 3/12 connectivity check.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Maria Delgado <maria.delgado@pangeaanalytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tomas Rivera <tomas.rivera@pangeaanalytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC MAP: Infrastructure Decisions & Owners (VPC, SSO, KMS)

Hi Kimberly —

Appreciate the concise MAP. A few clarifications from our side so we can align with security: 

- Identity: We do use Okta (enterprise) and can provide SAML metadata. SCIM provisioning is not enabled for third-party apps in our current plan; enabling SCIM would need an internal change and may push dates ~1–2 weeks. For the POC, we’d prefer a SAML-only flow (manual user provisioning) unless Redwood needs SCIM for automation.
- KMS: Our security lead prefers BYO-CMK (AWS KMS) for any test keys that touch customer data. We understand envelope encryption options but need an assurance on key usage policies and audit logs.
- Network: We can do VPC peering for staging; will need to confirm CIDR ranges. Peering is simpler for our infra team.

We’ll aim to confirm IdP metadata and a contact for our security team by Monday 3/08. Also, can you send a short checklist of the audit artifacts Redwood can provide (audit logs, access logs, token retention) so our compliance folks can sign off?

Thanks,
Maria
Head of Security & Ops | Pangea Analytics
maria.delgado@pangeaanalytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Delgado <maria.delgado@pangeaanalytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC MAP: Infrastructure Decisions & Owners (VPC, SSO, KMS)

Maria / team —

Thanks for the quick response — glad peering works. A couple of operational notes from our side: 

- On KMS: we support BYO-CMK for Private deployments; for the hosted POC we can run with envelope keys but we will document how CMKs would be used and the audit trails produced. I’ll attach a short checklist for the security artifacts (SOC2 scoping, audit log retention, token lifecycle).
- Connectivity test: I propose Redwood run a minimal connectivity smoke on 3/12 (09:00–11:00 PT). Ben will own the test and share results + commands. Karthik / Laura will be on standby if any peering/routing updates are needed.
- Timeline: if we get SAML metadata by 3/08 and CIDRs by 3/09, we should be able to provision peering and IP allowlists by 3/11 and do the smoke on 3/12 — keeps us on track for the 4/15 POC window.

Action items I’m picking up:
- Draft security artifact checklist (Ben) — will share in separate email by EOD 3/05.
- Connectivity test invitation (Ben) — will send calendar invite for 3/12.
- Routing/peering playbook (Karthik) — will add to the Drive folder.

Ben

Thanks all — quick confirmations and next steps below. I’ve updated the MAP (attached) with the owners Ben and Karthik called out and a short dependency table for the SSO/KMS decisions.

Summary/confirmation: 
- SSO: Pangea will start with SAML (manual provisioning). Okta metadata due by 2027-03-08.
- KMS: Pangea prefers BYO-CMK; Redwood to provide envelope-key integration doc and audit artifacts for security review.
- Network: VPC peering agreed for staging; Tomas to share CIDRs by 2027-03-09.
- Connectivity smoke: 2027-03-12 09:00 PT — Ben to send invite.

I’ve also added a short escalation path in the MAP (who to loop in if network or key management stalls). Please review the updated MAP in Drive and post any edits directly to the spreadsheet. If no blockers, we’ll lock owners in the MAP on 2027-03-10 and move to provisioning.
